title: the I/O ports of the PC
covers: The I/O ports of the PC as the list's port map gives them: what each port is and does, with what DOSBox-X does at it. The register tables behind a chipset's index port belong to that chip, not here.

rows.text: Ports 0000h-0007h hold the current address, base address and word count of DMA channels 0-3.
A read of an even port 0000h-0006h gives a channel's current address, one byte per read.
A write of 0000h-0007h sets a channel's base address and word count, the low byte first.
A read of 0008h gives the status of channels 0-3.
Ports 0008h-000Bh hold the command, write request, mask and mode registers.
Ports 000Ch-000Fh clear the byte pointer flip-flop, hold the temporary register, reset the 8237, clear the masks and write the mask bits.
Channel 2 serves the floppy, channel 0 refreshed memory on the PC/XT, channel 3 served the XT hard disk and channel 4 cascades on ATs.
The temporary register holds the last byte transferred in a memory-to-memory DMA transfer.
The command and request registers do not exist on a PS/2 DMA controller.
A byte handler is installed for each of ports 0000h-000Fh of the first controller.
Ports 0010h-001Fh are the 8237 DMA controller's registers on PS/2 models 60 and 80.
0018h is the extended function register and 001Ah the extended function execute register.
A write of 0018h sets the extended function register, and a write of 001Ah executes the function.
A one-byte read of a port that no device answers reaches IO_ReadBlocked, which returns all ones.
A one-byte write of a port that no device answers reaches IO_WriteBlocked, whose body is empty.
A write of 0018h and 001Ah stores nothing: it reaches IO_WriteBlocked, an empty body.
Ports 0020h-003Fh are the first 8259A programmable interrupt controller's.
A write of 0020h issues ICW1, OCW2 or OCW3 to the controller.
A read of 0020h after OCW3 gives the interrupt request or in-service register.
Each bit of that register holds one interrupt line: 1 an active request or a line in service.
A write of 0021h issues ICW2-ICW4 after ICW1, or sets the mask register OCW1.
A read of 0021h gives the master interrupt mask register.
read_command and write_command answer port 0020h, read_data and write_data port 0021h.
Port 0022h is the Intel 82439TX chipset's power control register.
A read of 0022h gives the PM2 register block.
A write of 0022h sets the PM2 register block.
Bits 7-1 of the register are reserved.
Bit 0 is the Arbiter Disable bit.
A byte read of a port with no handler enters IO_ReadSlowPath, which picks IO_ReadBlocked for a one-byte access.
A byte write of a port with no handler enters IO_WriteSlowPath, which picks IO_WriteBlocked, whose body does nothing.
The one-byte handler returns all ones, and IO_ReadB truncates it, so a byte read gives 0xFF.
The write reaches IO_WriteBlocked, an empty body: nothing is stored.
No bit of the register is stored, the write reaching an empty body.
The Arbiter Disable bit is not stored and disables nothing, the write reaching an empty body.

XT and AT use ports 0040h-0043h; PS/2 uses 0040h, 0042h-0044h and 0047h.
The counter chip is driven at 1.193 MHz, a quarter of the PC's 4.77 MHz clock.
A read of 0040h-0042h gives a counter's current value, one byte at a time.
In read back mode the counters and their status are latched, and in get-status mode the first byte read is the status.
A 16-bit read without the latch command takes the high and low parts at the instant of the port read, so they can wrap.
A control word written to 0043h must be followed at once by the counter action, or the system may hang.
A write of 0040h-0042h sets a counter's value, the low byte first in 16-bit mode.
A write of 0043h is the mode port, the control word register of counters 0-2.
Counter 0 keeps the system time: divisor 0000h gives the 18.2 Hz tick.
Counter 1 is the RAM refresh counter and counter 2 the cassette and speaker timer.
Counter 1 must not be set below 3, and is best left alone.
write_latch answers a write of 0040h and 0042h, write_p43 a write of 0043h, and read_latch a read of 0040h-0042h.
A write of 0040h or 0042h sets its counter, but 0041h is not installed: its write reaches IO_WriteBlocked.

The eight ports are data, error or write precompensation, sector count, sector number or LBA low, cylinder low and high or LBA middle and high, drive/head, status or command.
In diagnostic mode bits 2-0 give an error code and bit 7 the failed drive; in operation mode bit 7 is a bad block and bit 6 an ECC error.
The drive/head register's bit 6 enables LBA mode, bit 4 selects the drive and bits 3-0 hold the head or LBA bits 27-24.
The status register's bit 7 says a command is executing, bit 6 the drive is ready, bit 3 the sector buffer needs service and bit 0 the previous command failed.
The command codes include NOP (00h), device reset (08h), recalibrate (1xh), read sectors (20h-23h), write sectors (30h-33h) and write verify (3Ch).
Further codes are read verify (40h, 41h), format track (50h), seek (7xh), vendor unique 3 (8xh), execute diagnostics (90h) and initialize drive parameters (91h).
Then download microcode (92h), standby and idle (94h-97h), check power mode (98h), sleep (99h), the packet command (A0h), ATAPI identify (A1h) and SMART (B0h).
Then vendor unique 2 (C0h-C3h), read and write multiple (C4h, C5h), set multiple (C6h), the DMA commands, media status and the removable-media commands (DBh-DFh).
The last codes are buffer commands (E4h, E8h), write same (E9h), the security commands (EAh-EFh), the EATA commands and vendor unique 4 (F5h-FFh).
The identify-drive reply's first words give the general configuration, logical cylinders, heads and sectors, and marks 08h-12h vendor-specific.
The reply carries a blank-padded serial number at 14h, a buffer type and size, the long-read ECC byte count and a blank-padded firmware revision at 2Eh.
A blank-padded model number sits at 36h; 5Eh gives the read/write multiple count, 60h marks doubleword support and 62h the capabilities.
Word 64h gives the security mode, 66h and 68h the PIO and single-word DMA timings, 6Ah the field validity and 6Ch-72h the current translation and capacity.
Word 76h gives the multiple-sector count, 78h the LBA sector total, 7Ch and 7Eh the single-word and multiword DMA mode bitmaps, 80h the flow-control PIO modes.
The reply gives DMA and PIO cycle times at 82h-88h, reserved words at 8Ah-90h and 94h-99h, command queueing at 92h and the ATA revision at A0h and A2h.
Feature-set words at A4h-AEh report support and enablement, B0h-DFh and 140h-1FFh are reserved, 100h-13Fh vendor-specific, and 100h also holds the security status.
The general configuration word's bit 15 is the device class, bits 10-8 the transfer rate, bits 7-6 the drive type and bit 3 the encoding.
The capabilities word reports the standby timer (bit 13), IORDY (bit 11), its disabling (bit 10), LBA mode (bit 9) and DMA (bit 8).
The feature-set words report commands and features by bit, from SMART (bit 0) and security (bit 1) to identify-device-DMA support (bit 15), with 0000h and FFFFh meaning unsupported.
Feature-set support 2 has bit 14 set and bit 15 clear when supported, the extension reserves bits 13-0, and feature-set enabled 1 lists what is enabled.
The enabled-1 word continues with the SMART bit at 0, and the command queueing word gives the maximum depth in bits 4-0.
The ATAPI identify reply gives the configuration at 00h, vendor words at 02h and 28h, a serial at 14h, a firmware revision at 2Eh and a model at 36h.
It continues with vendor-specific and reserved words, security mode at 64h, timings at 66h and 68h, validity at 6Ah and the translated geometry and capacity.
The ATAPI configuration word gives the device type in bits 15-14, the ATAPI type in bits 12-8, removability in bit 7 and the packet size in bits 1-0.
ATAPI device type 00h is a disk, 01h a tape, 05h a CD-ROM, 07h optical memory, 08h a changer and 1Fh an unknown type or no device.
The SMART subcommands D0h and D1h read the attribute values and thresholds, D2h toggles autosave, D4h runs off-line tests and DAh returns the status.
The SMART thresholds sector holds a revision word, thirty 12-byte attribute records, reserved and vendor bytes and a checksum in the last byte.
The SMART values sector has the same shape plus the off-line collection status, time, capability and the SMART capabilities word at 170h.
SMART capabilities bit 0 says attributes are saved on power-down and bit 1 that the autosave subcommands are supported.
A SMART attribute threshold record is an ID byte, a threshold byte (00h always passing, FFh always failing) and ten reserved bytes.
A SMART attribute value record is an ID byte, a status-flags word (bit 0 pre-failure, bit 1 on-line collection), a value byte and vendor bytes.

Mix control bits 5-0 enable MIDI loopback, combine the GF1 and MIDI IRQs, enable the latches and MIC IN, and disable LINE OUT and LINE IN.
IRQ status bits 7, 6, 5, 3, 2, 1 and 0 report the DMA TC, volume ramp, WaveTable, timer 2, timer 1, MIDI receive and MIDI transmit IRQs.
Timer data bit 7 resets the timer IRQ, bit 6 masks timer 1, bit 5 masks timer 2, bit 1 starts timer 2 and bit 0 starts timer 1.
IRQ control bit 6 combines both IRQs; bits 5-3 select the MIDI IRQ and bits 2-0 the GF1 IRQ, each none or IRQ 2, 5, 3, 7, 11, 12, 15.
DMA control bit 6 combines both DMAs; bits 5-3 select DMA channel 2 and bits 2-0 channel 1, each none or DMA 1, 3, 5, 6, 7.

Ports 0330h-0331h are the default address of the MPU-401 MIDI UART: 0300h is the alternate and 0310h or 0320h turn up occasionally.
0330h is the data register; 0331h is the status register on read and the command register on write.
The MPU-401 generates an interrupt when MIDI code is ready, and reading the data register clears it.
In the status register bit 7 is input ready (1: no data available) and bit 6 output ready (1: not ready to receive); bits 5-0 are reserved.
The list adds that a pending input seems to block the output.
The command set includes 01h send MIDI stop, 02h start, 03h continue and 15h stop all recording, playback and MIDI.
It then has 34h return timing bytes in stop mode, 35h, 38h and 39h enable mode, common and real-time messages, and 3Ch and 3Dh choose CLS or SMPTE sync.
3Fh enters UART mode, 80h-84h choose MIDI or FSK sync and the metronome, 87h enables pitch and controller, and 8Ah-8Ch choose stop-mode data and measure-end messages.
91h enables extended MIDI control, 94h and 95h disable and enable the clock to host, and 97h enables system exclusive messages.
ACh and ADh return the MIDI version and the revision, Cxh sets the timebase to x*24 ppqn, and D0h and DFh are marked ???.
E0h sets the tempo, E4h the clocks per click, E6h the beats per measure and E7h sends all clocks to host.
FFh resets the MPU-401; after a command byte the MPU-401 must reply with the acknowledge byte FEh in the data register.
No command but reset can be issued in UART mode, and the MPU-401 must be reset to leave it.
The table's key makes ACK the acknowledge byte FEh, VER and REV the version and revision, BPS beats per second (8..250), CPC clocks per click and BPM beats per measure.

The status register's bits are self-test, diagnostic failure, mailbox initialization required, adapter idle, command full, data full and invalid command.
Bit 0 is valid only after a command complete interrupt; reading the data in register resets bit 2 and writing needs bit 3 clear.
Bit 4 says no commands are outstanding, bit 5 that mailbox initialization is required, and bit 7 clears when diagnostics finish.
The control register's bits are hardware reset, software reset, interrupt reset and SCSI bus reset; bits 3-0 are reserved.
Bit 4 asserts SCSI RST for 25 microseconds as a soft reset; bit 5 clears the interrupts and bit 6 cancels ongoing commands.
Bit 7 forces a power-on reset that reruns diagnostics and loses all SCSI status; when a reset completes, status bits 4 and 5 are set.
The interrupt status register's bit 7 is any interrupt and bits 3-0 are SCSI reset, command complete, mailbox out available and mailbox in full.
The notes say the mailbox interrupts wait until command complete and SCSI reset detected are cleared.
Command codes 00h-04h are no operation, mailbox initialization, start SCSI command, start PC/AT BIOS command and adapter inquiry.

03B4h-03B5h reach the CRT index and data handlers once a write of 03C2h selects the mono base at 03B0h.

Ports 03BCh-03BFh are the parallel printer port that MDA's LPT1 uses; the base may be 0278h, 0378h or 03BCh.
03BCh writes the data port and, on a bidirectional port, reads the connector's input.
03BDh reads the status port and 03BEh reads or writes the control port.
The status port reports busy, acknowledge, out of paper, selection, error, interrupt and reserved bits.
The control port sets the interrupt, printer select, initialize, line feed and strobe lines.
The parallel port object installs its data, status and control handlers at whatever base the configuration sets.
With printer support built in, parallel1 defaults to the printer type, and the first parallel port is created at 0378h, its handlers installed there.

03BFh is the Hercules configuration switch register, also found on EGA and VGA clones in Hercules emulation.
On ET4000 it is the Hercules compatibility register and on Genoa SuperEGA the miscellaneous register.
Bits 1-0 of the configuration register disable or enable the upper 32K buffer and graphics mode.
The ET4000 compatibility register's bit 1 enables the upper 32K buffer, and AAh as the second key byte reaches extra registers at 03D8h.
On machine=hercules, a write of 03BFh reaches write_hercules, which stores it in vga.herc.enable_bits.

03C0h is the EGA/VGA attribute controller index and data register; each write toggles the index/data flipflop.
A read of input status 1 resets the flipflop to load the index; changes during vertical retrace do not flicker.
The index register's bit 5 selects CPU access with the screen dark or video access, and bits 4-0 select one of 32 registers.
03C1h reads the selected attribute register on VGA.
The indexed registers are sixteen palette registers, mode control, overscan, color enable, pixel panning and color select.
A palette register selects primary and secondary red, green and blue video.
The mode control register selects pages, pixel clock, panning, blink, line graphics, mono and graphics.
The EGA overscan register selects secondary and primary red, green and blue border color.
The VGA overscan register selects secondary and primary intensity and red, green and blue border color.
The color enable register selects the diagnostic video status and enables planes 3-0.
A write of 03C0h reaches write_p3c0, which stores the loaded index or dispatches the data to the selected attribute register.
A read of 03C0h reaches read_p3c0 and returns the index latch and the screen-off bit.
A read of 03C1h reaches read_p3c1 and returns the selected attribute register.
The miscellaneous registers of the EGA and VGA are captured between 03C2h and 03CFh.
03C2h reads input status 0 and writes the miscellaneous output register.
Input status 0 reports the vertical retrace interrupt, feature control, monitor sense and reserved bits.
The miscellaneous output register sets sync polarity, page select, clock, CPU access and the CRTC port address.
A write of 03C3h selects the video subsystem at 03C3h or 46E8h.
A read of 03C3h gives the video subsystem enable bits.
With no device at 03C3h, a write stores nothing: IO_WriteBlocked, the default handler, has an empty body.
With no device at 03C3h, a read gives 0FFh: IO_ReadBlocked returns all ones and IO_ReadB truncates it.
A write of 03C2h reaches write_p3c2, which stores it in vga.misc_output and registers the CRT and status handlers at the selected base.
A read of 03C2h reaches read_p3c2, which builds its value from the machine, the misc output and the retrace flag.

Ports 03C4h-03C5h are the EGA/VGA sequencer registers.
03C4h is the EGA write-only TS index register, or the VGA read/write sequencer index.
03C5h is the EGA write-only TS data register, or the VGA read/write sequencer data register.
The sequencer registers are reset, clocking mode, map mask, character map select, memory mode and the undocumented horizontal counter reset.
The clocking mode register sets refresh, shift load, character clock, serial load, bandwidth and dot clocks per character.
The map mask register enables writes to display memory planes 3-0.
The character map select register chooses the first and second text fonts by their offset in font memory.
The memory mode register sets chain 4, odd/even addressing, extended memory and text mode.
A write of 03C4h reaches write_p3c4, which masks the value and stores it as the sequencer index.
A read of 03C4h reaches read_p3c4 and returns the sequencer index.
A write of 03C5h reaches write_p3c5, which stores the selected sequencer register.
A read of 03C5h reaches read_p3c5 and returns the selected sequencer register.
Ports 03C6h-03C9h are the EGA/VGA/MCGA DAC registers.
03C6h is the PEL mask register, default FFh, ANDed with the color register address on VGA.
On HiColor ET4000, four consecutive reads of 03C6h followed by 80h enable the HiColor feature.
03C7h sets read mode and the first color register index for reads of 03C9h.
On CEG VGA with Edsun RAMDACs, three key sequences ('CEG', 'EDS', 'UNx') written in read mode to 03C9h register DEh enable Continuous Edge Graphics mode.
A read of 03C7h gives the DAC state: write cycle or read cycle.
03C8h sets write mode and the first color register index for writes of 03C9h.
On Genoa SuperEGA, 03C8h is a control register selecting EGA or backward compatibility mode.
On S3 Trio32 and Trio64, 03C8h reads a general input port.
03C9h reads or writes red, green and blue in three accesses, and the DAC index advances after each third access.
The CEG modes give x values 0-15 with their color counts, mixing and effective colors.
The CEG mixing codes give the new and old color ratios for modes A-D.
A read of 03C6h reaches read_p3c6 and returns the PEL mask.
A write of 03C6h reaches write_p3c6, which stores the PEL mask or the HiColor register.
A write of 03C7h reaches write_p3c7, which sets read mode and the read and write indices.
A read of 03C7h reaches read_p3c7 and returns 03h in read mode, else 00h.
A write of 03C8h reaches write_p3c8, which sets write mode and the write index.
A read of 03C8h reaches read_p3c8 and returns the write index.
A write of 03C9h reaches write_p3c9, which stores the red, green and blue components and advances after each third byte.
A read of 03C9h reaches read_p3c9 and returns the red, green and blue components in three reads.
03CAh writes the EGA graphics 2 position register and reads the VGA feature control register.
03CBh is an ET4000/W32 GDC segment select register for read and write segment pointers.
03CCh writes the EGA graphics 1 position register and reads the VGA miscellaneous output register.
03CDh is an ET3000, ET4000 or ET4000/W32 GDC segment select register for read and write segment pointers.
A read of 03CAh reaches read_p3ca, which returns 0.
A read of 03CCh reaches read_p3cc, which returns vga.misc_output.

03CEh is the EGA write-only GDC index register and the VGA read/write graphics address register.
03CFh is the EGA write-only GDC data register and the VGA read/write graphics data register.
The indexed registers are set/reset, enable set/reset, color compare, data rotate, read map select, mode, miscellaneous, color don't care, bit mask and the Paradise lock.
The enable set/reset register selects the planes whose set/reset value is used.
The color compare register holds a 4-bit color number in bits 3-0.
The data rotate register selects the logical function and the rotate count.
The mode register selects 256 colors, shift mode, odd/even, read mode and write mode.
The miscellaneous register selects the memory map, odd/even chaining and text or graphics mode.
A write of 03CEh reaches write_p3ce, which stores the low four bits as the GDC index.
A read of 03CEh reaches read_p3ce and returns the GDC index.
A write of 03CFh reaches write_p3cf, which dispatches on the GDC index and stores the register's fields.
A read of 03CFh reaches read_p3cf and returns the selected GDC register.

A write of 03D0h or 03D2h acts as a write of 03D4h.
A read of 03D1h or 03D3h acts as a read of 03D5h.
A write of 03D1h or 03D3h acts as a write of 03D5h.

With no device at 03D0h-03D3h, a write stores nothing: IO_WriteBlocked, the default handler, has an empty body.

03D4h is the CRT 6845 index register for CGA, MCGA, color EGA and color VGA, read/write on some VGAs.
03D5h is the CRT data register, selected by 03D4h; registers 0Ch-0Fh may be read and EGA/VGA registers reach 18h.
Registers 00h-0Fh repeat the MDA table, and 10h-11h are start and end vertical retrace in native VGA.
Registers 12h-18h are vertical display end, row offset, underline location, blanking start and end, mode control and line compare.
Genoa SuperEGA adds a double-scan control at 19h, Elsa a page select at 1Dh-1Eh, and VGA has the CPU latch and attribute toggle at 22h and 24h.
The attribute toggle register gives the current attribute index, palette address source and flipflop state.
MCGA redefines registers 10h-14h as mode control, interrupt control, character generator, font pointer and character count.
The MCGA mode control register sets sync suppression, dot clock, refresh calculation and video modes 11h and 13h.
The MCGA mode control status reports the CGA mode bit, clock rate, text mode, double scan and video modes 11h and 13h.
The MCGA interrupt control register selects tristate output, interrupt generation, handling and latch.
The MCGA character generator register selects the generator, codepage load timing, 512 characters and sync polarity.
A write of 03C2h selects the color base and registers the 03D4h-03D5h CRT handlers and the 03DAh status read.
A write of 03D4h reaches vga_write_p3d4, which stores the value as the CRT index.
A read of 03D4h reaches vga_read_p3d4 and returns the CRT index.
A write of 03D5h reaches vga_write_p3d5, which dispatches on the CRT index and stores the register's fields.
Ports 03D6h-03D7h are CGA mirrors of ports 03D4h and 03D5h.
Under OS/2, reads of 03D6h return 0 in a full-screen DOS session and nonzero in a windowed one.
A write of 03D6h acts as a write of 03D4h and a write of 03D7h as a write of 03D5h.
A read of 03D7h acts as a read of 03D5h.
With no device at 03D6h-03D7h, a write stores nothing: IO_WriteBlocked, the default handler, has an empty body.
With no device at 03D6h-03D7h, a read gives 0FFh: IO_ReadBlocked returns all ones and IO_ReadB truncates it.
On machine=ega, a write of 03C2h registers the four index and data pairs from the selected base; on machine=cga, pcjr, tandy, olivetti or 3270pc the 03D0h pairs are installed too.

A one-byte write of a port that no device answers reaches IO_WriteBlocked, whose body is empty.
03D8h is the CGA mode control register, absent from native color EGA and VGA but present on most clones.
03D9h is the CGA palette register, or the MCGA border control register, found on most clones.
03DAh reads the CGA status register, or input status 1 on color EGA and VGA.
03DAh writes the color EGA and VGA feature control register, also reachable at 03BAh in mono mode.
On the HZ309 card, bit 0 of 03DAh overrides the CRT beam control of 03D8h bit 3.
03DBh clears the light pen latch.
03DCh presets the light pen latch, or sets it on CGA.
03DDh is the MCGA extended mode control register, holding the DAC active, Plantronics and 256-color bits.
03DEh is reserved on MCGA and the AT&T mode control register on AT&T and color ET4000 cards.
03DFh is reserved on MCGA and the CRT/CPU page register on the PCjr.
The CGA mode control register sets the page, blink, 640x200 graphics, video, monochrome, text and column bits.
The CGA status register reports vertical sync, diagnostic feedback, retrace, light pen and horizontal retrace.
The CGA palette register selects the color set and the intense and border colors.
The color EGA and VGA feature control register sets NMI, vsync selection and feature connector control.
The AT&T mode control register sets underline color, alternate page and font, and double scan.
A read of 03DAh reaches vga_read_p3da, which builds the status from the frame timing and the display-enable flag.
On machine=cga, mcga, amstrad, olivetti or 3270pc, writes of 03D8h and 03D9h reach write_cga.
A one-byte read of a port that no device answers reaches IO_ReadBlocked, which returns all ones.
A one-byte write of a port that no device answers reaches IO_WriteBlocked, whose body is empty.
Ports 03F0h-03F7h are the first floppy disk controller, an 8272, 8272A, NEC765 or 82072 or 82077AA for 2.88M recording.
03F0h is diskette controller status A on PS/2 models, or the 82072AA's board jumper settings.
03F1h is diskette controller status B on PS/2 models.
03F2h is the diskette controller digital output register (DOR).
03F3h is the tape drive register on the 82077AA, selecting a tape drive or none.
03F4h reads the diskette controller main status register.
03F4h writes the diskette controller data rate select register.
03F5h reads a status register or the data register.
03F5h writes the diskette controller command register.
03F6h is reserved on the floppy controller and the fixed disk controller's data register.
03F6h writes the fixed disk controller's data register.
03F7h reads the digital input register, whose bit 7 reports a diskette change.
03F7h writes the configuration control register's data rate, with a fixed disk drive 0 select conflict.
Status A reports the interrupt, drive 2, step, track 0, head 1, index, write protect and direction.
Status A on the PS/2 model 30 reports interrupt, DRQ, step, track 0, head 1, index, write protect and direction.
The EHD controller jumper settings give the drive type for each of four drives.
Status B reports drive select, write and read data, write enable and motor enables.
Status B on the PS/2 model 30 reports drive 2, drive selects, data and write enable flipflops.
The DOR sets motor enables, DMA enable, controller reset and drive select.
The PS/2 digital input register reports diskette change, data rate and high density select.
The PS/2 model 30 digital input register reports diskette change, DMA gate, NOPREC and data rate.
The main status register reports RQM, transfer direction, non-DMA mode, busy and drive busy bits.
The data rate select register sets software reset, power down, write precompensation and data rate.
ST0 reports the last command status, seek completion, equipment check, ready, head and unit.
ST1 reports end of cylinder, CRC error, overrun, sector not found, write protect and address mark not found.
ST2 reports deleted address mark, CRC error, wrong cylinder, scan conditions, bad cylinder and missing address mark.
ST3 reports fault, write protect, ready, track zero, two-sided, side and unit select.
The fixed disk data register bits select reduced write current, head 3, reset and initialization.
The hard disk controller register selects write gate, head 3, heads 2-0 and drives 1-0.
The diskette command table gives the opcode and length of each command, from read track to relative seek.
The controller chip identification table maps version and partid values to their chips.
A write of 03F2h reaches fdc_baseio_w and on_dor_change, which stores it in digital_output_register.
A read of 03F4h reaches fdc_baseio_r's main status case and main_status's status bits.
A write of 03F4h reaches set_data_rate and, with bit 7 set, on_reset.
Reads and writes of 03F5h reach fdc_data_read and fdc_data_write, which return results and start commands.
A read of 03F7h reaches digital_input_register and a write reaches set_data_rate.
A read of 03F0h or 03F1h gives status A or B only in the PS/2 modes; otherwise the case falls through to 0FFh.
Ports 03F0h-03F1h are a PCTech RZ1000 IDE controller.
Two successive 8-bit OUTs of 55h to 03F0h unlock the ports; then 03F0h indexes the data at 03F1h until AAh is written.
An unlocked write of 03F0h selects the register accessed through 03F1h.
A read of 03F1h gives the selected register's data.
A write of 03F1h sets the selected register's data.
The RZ1000's registers 00h-05h are undefined and AAh locks the control port.
With the floppy controller at 03F0h, a one-byte write reaches fdc_baseio_w's default branch, which stores nothing.
With the floppy controller at 03F1h, a one-byte write reaches fdc_baseio_w's default branch, which stores nothing.
In the PC/AT mode, a read of 03F1h falls out of the status B case and returns 0FFh.
03F0h and 03F1h are installed by the floppy controller, whose status and data registers live there.
A write of 03F0h or 03F1h reaches fdc_baseio_w's default branch, which only logs it.
Ports 03F8h-03FFh are a serial port (8250, 8250A, 8251, 16450, 16550 or 16550A), COM1.
The 8250 was specified to 56Kbd and mostly runs 9600Bd; the 8250A, 16450 and 16C451 run to 115KBd; the 16550A has a working FIFO.
03F8h is the transmit and receive register or the divisor latch low byte, 03F9h the divisor latch high byte or interrupt enable register.
03FAh is the interrupt identification register or FIFO control register, 03FBh the line control register, 03FCh the modem control register.
03FDh is the line status register, 03FEh the modem status register and 03FFh the scratch register.
The divisor latch gives the divisor for each standard baud rate from 50 to 115200.
The interrupt enable register selects modem status, receiver line status, transmitter empty and received data interrupts.
The interrupt identification register reports the FIFO state and the highest-priority pending interrupt.
The FIFO control register sets the trigger level and clears or enables the receiver and transmitter FIFOs.
The line control register sets the divisor latch, break, parity, stop bits and word length.
The modem control register sets loopback, OUT2 and OUT1, request to send and data terminal ready.
The line status register reports transmitter empty, break, framing, parity and overrun errors and data ready.
The modem status register reports carrier detect, ring indicator, data set ready, clear to send and their deltas.
A read of 03F8h-03FFh reaches SERIAL_Read, which dispatches the register index to the COM1 object.
A write of 03F8h-03FFh reaches SERIAL_Write, which dispatches the register index to the COM1 object.
serial1 defaults to the dummy type, and its base is serial_defaultaddr[0], 03F8h, where its handlers are installed.
